text: Lesson 16 covered a notification's trigger and recipients — the when and the who. The what-does-the-email-actually-say part lives in a completely separate object: an Email Template, stored on sysevent_email_template. A notification record carries a field pointing at a template, rather than writing its own subject and body directly, and that separation is deliberate, not incidental.

Reuse is the whole point of splitting these apart. Picture five incident notifications — assignment, comment added, resolution, reopening, SLA warning — each with its own hand-written HTML body. A simple request, like adding a new support phone number to the footer, now means editing five records and hoping none of them drift out of sync. With one shared template, that same request becomes a single edit that applies everywhere it's referenced.

Templates aren't static text. Subject and body contain field placeholders, written as a dollar sign and curly braces around a field name, like short underscore description or priority or assigned underscore to. At send time, ServiceNow resolves every placeholder against the real record that triggered the notification, so one generic template produces a different, accurate email for every record it's used on, without a single line of script.

A template record carries three real pieces: a Subject field, which can itself contain placeholders; a Message HTML field for the rich body most email clients render, with headings and basic styling; and a plain-text fallback for clients or situations where HTML doesn't render. The practical habit is writing the HTML body first, then confirming the plain-text version still reads sensibly on its own.

Wiring a finished template to a notification is one reference field on the notification form. Pick the template, and that notification now sends exactly that subject and body whenever its trigger fires. The notification can still add extra content around it for links or context specific to that one notification, but the shared template is what the organization maintains centrally, in one place.

One template, many notifications, one place to edit when the wording needs to change. Next up: Inbound Email Actions — what actually happens on ServiceNow's side when someone hits reply on one of these notification emails.
